articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft's April patch party fixes a whopping 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and 'BlueHammer' in Windows Defender. When your monthly security update looks like a phone book, maybe it's time to rethink some architectural choices.

articles.title: PCPJack Credential Stealer Exploits 5 CVEs to Spread Worm-Like Across Cloud Systems
articles.summary: Ivanti's EPMM gets pwned again with CVE-2026-6973, granting admin-level RCE to attackers who barely had to try. At this point, Ivanti vulnerabilities are less 'zero-day' and more 'any-day-ending-in-y'.

articles.title: ThreatsDay Bulletin: Edge Plaintext Passwords, ICS 0-Days, Patch-or-Die Alerts and 25+ New Stories
articles.summary: PAN-OS buffer overflow (CVE-2026-0300) turns Palo Alto firewalls into espionage platforms with root access. Nothing says 'enterprise security' like your firewall becoming the front door for nation-state actors.

articles.title: Open Source is the Tip of the Iceberg: Why Proprietary Software, Hardware and Protocols Face Greater AI-Driven Security Risk
articles.summary: Palo Alto's User-ID Authentication Portal gets exploited in the wild through another critical RCE. Their firewalls are becoming less 'impenetrable wall' and more 'welcome mat with flashing neon arrows'.

articles.title: Germany Doxes “UNKN,” Head of RU Ransomware Gangs REvil, GandCrab
articles.summary: Russian military intelligence turns ancient router vulnerabilities into a Microsoft Office token harvesting operation. When your IoT becomes FSB's personal authentication candy store, maybe those firmware updates weren't so optional after all.

articles.title: One Click, Total Shutdown: The "Patient Zero" Webinar on Killing Stealth Breaches
articles.summary: PCPJack worm exploits 5 CVEs to spread across cloud systems like digital herpes, stealing credentials and evicting TeamPCP malware. Even malware is getting into turf wars now—it's a cybercriminal eat cybercriminal world out there.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: AI-Powered Phishing, Android Spying Tool, Linux Exploit, GitHub RCE & More
articles.summary: Instructure breach exposes 280 million education records from 8,800 schools and universities. Because nothing says 'protecting our children's future' like letting hackers mine their personal data like digital coal.

articles.title: After Replacing TeamPCP Malware, 'PCPJack' Steals Cloud Secrets
articles.summary: EFF channels William Binney's warning about the 'turnkey totalitarian state' as surveillance infrastructure awaits its next political master. The panopticon is fully operational—we just keep handing the keys to whoever wins elections.

articles.title: Milestone 1.0.0 Release of APK Downloader `apkeep` Powers Research on Android Apps
articles.summary: Germany doxes 'UNKN,' the Russian mastermind behind REvil and GandCrab ransomware empires responsible for 130+ cyberattacks. Daniil Shchukin's face is now public—proof that even digital ghosts eventually get their close-up.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider's 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud and identity theft in 2022 SMS phishing campaigns. Another young Brit learns that social engineering corporations is significantly less glamorous when federal prosecutors get involved.
